Subject: POC success criteria & next steps (recap)

Hi Emily / Devon

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed POC plan so we have alignment before we loop in CS and Security:

Goals (what success looks like)
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for 256-token responses under your expected request mix
- Throughput: sustain 150 qps for peak flows (burst to 300 qps)
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0008 (estimated with Redwood Optimize profiles)
- Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your rubric (intent recall + hallucination score) on a 1k-prompt eval set

Evaluation plan / ownership
- Redwood will provide eval harness + synthetic load driver to measure latency/throughput (owner: Jordan)
- Atlas provides representative sample prompts + 1k labeled eval set (owner: Emily / Dev)
- CS lead (Marissa) will run onboarding, config (batching, quantization) and monitor metrics during trial

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): exchange sample data + security questionnaire
- Week 1: account provisioning, baseline latency/throughput run, initial quality eval
- Weeks 2-5: POC trial (tuning, monitoring, daily syncs)
- Week 6: final evaluation, decision

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan.pdf (POC runbook)
I'll attach the plan and eval harness.

Open questions / asks from Atlas:
1) Can you share the sample prompt set and any redlines in the QA rubric by Monday (Aug 12)?
2) Procurement timeline / any required PO or MSA steps?
3) Which region do you want the trial hosted in (us / eu)?

Proposed next step: 30-min sync early next week to finalize sample data and timeline.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Thanks Jordan
 this is a helpful summary. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Latency: Is the p95 target measured at 256 tokens purely server-side (no network) or end-to-end (including client-side latency)? Also please note our typical prompt sizes average ~180 tokens, responses ~320 tokens.
- Quality rubric: can you share an example rubric or a template (we want to map to our internal risk scoring)?
- Monitoring: we'll need access to per-request traces and audit logs (for fraud review) during the trial. Is that available in the trial environment?

Procurement: procurement flagged that any PII handling and SOC2 evidence will be required before we move to an extended trial. I'll attach our vendor security checklist (vendor_security_requirements.xlsx)
 can your security team confirm whether Redwood can provide SOC2 and KMS integration details?

We can try to get the sample prompts to you by Mon (Aug 12) but procurement may push signing until week 2. Does that timeline still work?


Emily
Emily Zhao
Senior Product Manager, Atlas Payments

Emily
 good questions. Short answers: 

- Latency measurement: our baseline p95 is server-side measured at ingress/egress (including model execution and Redwood runtime overhead). We can run an end-to-end test from your region if you prefer; for the POC we'll include both server-side and client-side (p95) numbers. We typically report p50/p95/p99.
- Token sizing: we'll use your distribution (180/320) for the baseline runs
I'll note that in the plan.
- Monitoring & logs: trial accounts include request-level traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and an audit log export (S3). We can grant read-only access to those dashboards to your security and engineering teams.

I'll attach the eval harness we run (redwood_eval_harness.tar.gz) and the POC runbook (redwood_poc_plan.pdf). If procurement needs SOC2 before Week 2 I'll attach our standard SOC2 attestation for pre-review.

If procurement signing slips to Week 2 that's fine
 we'll still kickoff the baseline tests as soon as sample prompts are available. Proposed 30-min sync: Tue 2029-08-13 10:00am PT. Does that work for you?

Jordan

 for planning purposes only, rough numbers:
- Token estimate: 100M tokens at our Optimize profile (mixed prompt/response) => ballpark $8k-$12k for the 4-week POC depending on batching and quantization choices. We'll provide a more granular cost model once we have the exact token distribution.
- KMS: Redwood Private and Dedicated customers can use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For hosted trials we support encrypted logs with customer-managed KMS integration as an option
 we'll confirm specifics with Security.
- Data residency: audit log exports can be configured to land in your AWS account (region of your choosing)
 we'll include that in the runbook.
